content.text: Constructions
Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment using a compass and straightedge
Construct the angle bisector of a given angle
Construct an angle of $60°$ and $90°$ using a compass
Construct the perpendicular from a point to a line
Understand why constructions are more precise than measuring with a protractor
Introduction
Geometric constructions use only a
compass
and a
straightedge

(an unmarked ruler). No measurements are taken; the accuracy comes entirely from the properties of circles and straight lines. This tradition goes back to the ancient Greeks, who believed these were the purest tools for geometry. Constructions are still tested in GCSE and IGCSE examinations, and you will need to leave your construction arcs visible to earn full marks.
Key Concepts
Compass:
A tool for drawing arcs and circles of a fixed radius.
Straightedge:
A ruler used only for drawing straight lines (not for measuring).
Construction arcs:
The arcs drawn during a construction. You
must
leave these visible in your working. They prove that you used a compass and not a protractor.
Foundation and Higher:
Constructions are tested on both tiers. You must be able to perform them accurately and leave all construction arcs showing.
Construction 1: Perpendicular Bisector of a Line Segment
The
perpendicular bisector
of a line segment is a line that:
Passes through the
midpoint
of the segment
Is at
right angles
($90°$) to the segment
Method
Given line segment $AB$:
Open your compass to more than half the length of $AB$.
Place the compass point on $A$ and draw arcs above and below the line.
Without changing the compass width, place the compass point on $B$ and draw arcs above and below the line.
The two pairs of arcs intersect at two points. Draw a straight line through these two intersection points.
This line is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$. It passes through the midpoint $M$ of $AB$ and is perpendicular to $AB$.
Why it works:
The two intersection points are equidistant from $A$ and $B$. Any point equidistant from both endpoints lies on the perpendicular bisector.
Quick Check:
What does the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ tell you about any point $P$ on it?
$PA = PB$ (every point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from $A$ and $B$).
Construction 2: Angle Bisector
The
angle bisector
divides an angle into two equal parts.
Method
Given angle $\angle BAC$:
Place the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc that crosses both arms $AB$ and $AC$. Label the intersection points $P$ and $Q$.
Place the compass point on $P$ and draw an arc in the interior of the angle.
Without changing the compass width, place the compass point on $Q$ and draw another arc in the interior, crossing the arc from step 2. Label the intersection point $R$.
Draw a straight line from $A$ through $R$.
The line $AR$ bisects $\angle BAC$, so $\angle BAR = \angle RAC$.
Why it works:
Point $R$ is equidistant from both arms of the angle, so it lies on the angle bisector.
Construction 3: Constructing a $60°$ Angle
An equilateral triangle has all angles equal to $60°$. We use this fact.
Method
Given a ray from point $A$:
Place the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc crossing the ray. Label the intersection $B$.
Without changing the compass width, place the compass point on $B$ and draw an arc that crosses the first arc. Label this intersection $C$.
Draw a straight line from $A$ through $C$.
$\angle BAC = 60°$ because triangle $ABC$ is equilateral (all three sides equal the compass radius).
Quick Check:
How would you construct $30°$?
Construct $60°$, then bisect it using the angle bisector construction.
Construction 4: Constructing a $90°$ Angle
This is the same as constructing the perpendicular bisector, applied at a specific point.
Method 1: Perpendicular at a point on a line
Given a line and a point $P$ on it:
Place the compass on $P$ and draw arcs on both sides, marking points $A$ and $B$ on the line (equal distances from $P$).
Increase the compass width. From $A$, draw an arc above the line. From $B$, draw an arc above the line.
The arcs intersect at $C$. Draw a line from $P$ through $C$.
This line is perpendicular to the original line at $P$.
Method 2: Perpendicular from a point to a line
Given a line and a point $P$
not
on the line:
From $P$, draw an arc that crosses the line at two points $A$ and $B$.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ (as in Construction 1).
This perpendicular bisector passes through $P$ and meets the line at right angles.
Construction 5: Constructing Other Standard Angles
Using combinations of the constructions above:
Angle
Method
Equilateral triangle construction
Construct $60°$, then bisect
Perpendicular construction
Construct $90°$, then bisect
Construct $60°$ on both sides of the ray, or construct $60°$ and extend
Construct $180° - 30°$ or bisect $120°$ and $180°$
Worked Examples
Example 1: Perpendicular bisector
Question:
Draw a line segment $AB = 8$ cm. Construct its perpendicular bisector. Mark the midpoint $M$.
Solution:
Draw $AB = 8$ cm.
Set compass to more than $4$ cm (e.g., $5$ cm).
From $A$, draw arcs above and below.
From $B$ (same compass width), draw arcs above and below.
Join the two intersection points with a straight line.
This line crosses $AB$ at the midpoint $M$, where $AM = MB = 4$ cm.
The perpendicular bisector passes through $M$ at $90°$ to $AB$.
Example 2: Angle bisector
Question:
Draw an angle of approximately $70°$. Construct the angle bisector.
Solution:
Draw an angle of approximately $70°$ (using a protractor for the initial angle, then constructing the bisector).
From the vertex, draw an arc crossing both arms.
From each intersection point, draw arcs of equal radius inside the angle.
Join the vertex to the intersection of the two arcs.
Each half of the angle is $35°$.
Example 3: Constructing $60°$
Question:
Using only a compass and straightedge, construct an angle of $60°$ at point $A$ on line $l$.
Solution:
From $A$, draw an arc crossing line $l$ at point $B$.
Without changing the compass width, from $B$ draw an arc crossing the first arc at point $C$.
Draw line $AC$.
$\angle BAC = 60°$ (equilateral triangle: $AB = BC = AC$).
Example 4: Constructing $45°$
Question:
Construct an angle of $45°$ at a point on a line.
Solution:
First construct a $90°$ angle (perpendicular at the point).
Then bisect the $90°$ angle using the angle bisector construction.
Each half is $45°$.
Common Mistakes
Mistake
Why It's Wrong
Correct Approach
Rubbing out construction arcs
Arcs prove you used a compass; examiners need to see them
Always leave construction arcs visible
Changing the compass width during a construction
This invalidates the geometric reasoning
Keep the compass width fixed during each step
Setting the compass to less than half the line for perpendicular bisector
The arcs will not intersect
Open the compass to
more
than half the line length
Using a protractor instead of a compass
The question asks for a construction, not a measurement
Use compass and straightedge only
Drawing freehand arcs
This reduces accuracy
Always use the compass for arcs
Practice Questions
Foundation Level
Draw a line segment of $10$ cm. Construct the perpendicular bisector and verify that it passes through the midpoint ($5$ cm from each end).
Draw an angle of $80°$ (using a protractor). Construct the angle bisector. Measure each half to verify they are approximately $40°$.
Construct an equilateral triangle with side length $6$ cm using only a compass and straightedge.
Using constructions only, create an angle of $60°$.
Construct the perpendicular from a point $P$ (3 cm above a horizontal line) to the line.
Draw a line segment $AB = 7$ cm. Construct the perpendicular bisector. Mark any point $P$ on it and verify that $PA = PB$.
Higher Level
Construct an angle of $30°$ using only compass and straightedge. Describe your method.
Construct an angle of $45°$. Show all construction arcs.
Construct a $90°$ angle at a point that is
not
at the end of the line segment.
Given a triangle $ABC$, construct the perpendicular bisectors of all three sides. Verify they meet at a single point (the circumcentre).
Construct a $75°$ angle.
Given a line segment $AB = 9$ cm, construct a point $C$ such that $AC = BC$ and $\angle ACB = 60°$.
Answers
The perpendicular bisector should cross $AB$ at exactly $5$ cm from each end. The angle between the bisector and $AB$ should be $90°$.
Each half should measure approximately $40°$ when checked with a protractor.
Draw $AB = 6$ cm. From $A$ with radius $6$ cm, draw an arc. From $B$ with radius $6$ cm, draw an arc. The intersection $C$ gives equilateral triangle $ABC$.
Use the equilateral triangle construction from a point on a ray.
From $P$, draw an arc crossing the line at two points. Construct the perpendicular bisector of the two intersection points. This passes through $P$ and meets the line at $90°$.
By the property of perpendicular bisectors, any point on it is equidistant from $A$ and $B$, so $PA = PB$.
First construct $60°$ (equilateral triangle method). Then bisect the $60°$ angle using the angle bisector construction. Each half is $30°$.
Construct $90°$ (perpendicular at a point), then bisect it to get $45°$.
From the point $P$ on the line, mark equal distances on both sides ($A$ and $B$). Then construct the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, which passes through $P$.
The three perpendicular bisectors should meet at a single point (circumcentre). This point is equidistant from all three vertices.
Method: Construct $60°$, then construct a $90°$ at the same point. Bisect the $30°$ gap between $60°$ and $90°$ to get $15°$. Add to $60°$: $60° + 15° = 75°$.

Construct the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ (so $AC = BC$). On the bisector, find $C$ such that $\angle ACB = 60°$. Since $AC = BC$, triangle $ACB$ is isosceles with $\angle ACB = 60°$, making it equilateral, so $C$ is at distance $9$ cm from both $A$ and $B$.
Exam Tips
Leave all construction arcs visible.
This is the single most important thing. If you erase them, you will lose marks.
Use a sharp pencil for accuracy.
When constructing a perpendicular bisector, make the compass opening
clearly
more than half the line. Too close to half and the arcs barely intersect.
Practice each construction repeatedly until you can do it confidently under exam conditions.
Read the question carefully: "construct" means compass and straightedge only. "Draw" may allow a protractor.
Summary
Perpendicular bisector:
Arcs from both endpoints; join the intersection points. Creates a line through the midpoint at $90°$.
Angle bisector:
Arc from vertex, then equal arcs from the intersection points on the arms. Join vertex to new intersection.
$60°$ angle:
Use the equilateral triangle construction (all sides equal to compass radius).
$90°$ angle:
Perpendicular construction at a point on a line.
Bisect $60°$.
Bisect $90°$.
Always use a compass and straightedge, and
leave construction arcs visible
